- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate during mean-reversion phases; adjust upward if recent history shows persistent downward drift.
- Overshoot after spikes (e.g., 60+ → 70+), then fail to correct; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% above recent high.
- Lagging response to true price movements; delay correction by 1–2 periods; add 1–2% lagged true value to forecast.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices; apply downward adjustment of 2–5% for 30-day forecasts unless confirmed by macro signals.
- Avoid overfitting to recent volatility; if 3–5 consecutive days show high volatility, reduce forecast variance by 10–20%.
